summary_paragraph: Mr. ___ was admitted with altered mental status and tremors following a recent hospital discharge. Initial evaluation revealed no acute intracranial pathology, infection, or metabolic derangement. His confusion was attributed to delirium, likely exacerbated by medications including tolterodine and Celexa, which were discontinued. His myoclonic tremors were managed with an increase in Cymbalta and adjustment of trazodone. A positive urinalysis was determined to reflect colonization due to his chronic indwelling catheter, not infection, so antibiotics were avoided. Conjunctivitis and seborrheic dermatitis improved with targeted treatment. His blood pressure remained low, prompting discontinuation of lisinopril and furosemide. He regained baseline mental status, was stabilized on revised medications, and was discharged to extended care for rehabilitation with follow-up arranged in neurology, urology, and primary care.
